item.title: Jonathan Carver Moore Is Rewriting the Gallery Playbook
item.description: "I don’t see limits when I’m trying to do something, and I don’t think anyone should. If I had gone through the so-called proper channels, I don’t think I would have done things the way I have.”

item.title: Dana Walden Faces Disney’s Franchise and Streaming Reckoning
item.description: As Bob Iger exits and Josh D’Amaro ascends, Dana Walden becomes the key figure shaping Disney’s stories, franchises and streaming future.

item.title: The Enduring Appeal of John F. Kennedy Jr.’s All-American Style
item.description: As Ryan Murphy's 'Love Story' brings America's most photographed couple back to screen, a style retrospective proves John F. Kennedy Jr.'s wardrobe was always the real plot.

item.title: Steep Slopes and Silver Dollars: The Insider’s Guide to Jackson Hole
item.description: Whether line dancing at The Wort Hotel or skiing off-piste in the towering Teton Mountains, the Old West spirit prevails in Jackson Hole.

item.title: Don’t Miss: “Lee Miller” at Tate Britain
item.description: Some of the show’s most powerful images are from Miller’s travels around the Middle East, following her marriage to Egyptian businessman Aziz Eloui Bey.

item.title: Ali Gass On ICA San Francisco’s Shift to a Nomadic Model
item.description: The institution is rethinking what a museum can be by prioritizing experimentation, artistic production and public engagement over collection building.

item.title: A.I.’s Environmental Impact Is Testing Corporate Climate Commitments
item.description: Trilateral Research’s Dr. Rowena Rodrigues and Amelia Williams examine the widening gap between corporate sustainability claims and the measurable environmental impacts of A.I. Without integrated, lifecycle-based impact assessments, they argue, even well-intentioned organizations risk unintentional greenwashing.

item.title: Four Astronauts, One Giant Test: What’s at Stake for NASA’s Artemis II Moon Mission
item.description: More than 50 years after Apollo 17, NASA’s Artemis II will send four astronauts on a 10-day loop around the Moon to test the agency’s deep-space hardware.

item.title: John Kelly Ponders the Day His Art Nearly Crippled Him
item.description: In 182 illustrated panels on view at PPOW in New York, the artist recalls the traumatic 2002 accident that prompted him to reconsider the meaning and direction of his practice.

item.title: Hugging Face’s Monetization Chief Jeff Boudier Isn’t Interested in Chasing Money
item.description: Hugging Face’s Jeff Boudier reveals a contrarian approach to growth, profitability and trust in an A.I. industry obsessed with scale.
